items.note: Both plans carry B1 (net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c; B spells out the row algebra, A gives it with the cancellation reason), B2, B3 and B4, plus the neighbour and wire counts (paper 741-783). No substantive difference.

Both state the invariant (stored array = D_v applied to logical array), the commuting of a common frame with a pointwise linear gate, the operator D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} for all roles (paper 804-825).

differences.what: The per-edge orthogonal residual table: B lists the residuals of every edge (B(x)t_X-perp, P(x)t_X-perp on X; B(x)t_Y-perp, P(x)t_Y-perp on Y; B(x)F then P(x)F three times on a central wire; the four side-wire residuals; (A(x)F)(x)Q-perp on scratch sink edges; zero elsewhere). A gives only the gate-label table and the single side residual for edge 2->5, not the residual table.

Orthonormal bases over F_2: B states that each nonzero residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector, and that alternating planes are absorbed into a unit line via w+a, w+b, w+a+b. A states nondegenerate and nonalternating hence orthonormal basis, but justifies it by saying the residual contains a coordinate unit vector, whereas the paper's norm-one vector is a tensor of line vectors (P, Q) and coordinate units, which in general is not a coordinate unit vector; A omits the absorption of alternating planes.

items.note: L2, L3 and L5 are present in both (A states the 2->5 nesting more explicitly, B gives the h-2 residual with t_X perp t_Y). B additionally carries the residual table (L1) and a correct, complete L4, while A's L4 justification misstates the norm-one vector.
Both assign P_U and -P_{U_a}, show rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, add the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a}, check the endpoint difference I_m and give s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m (paper 1156-1171).

differences.what: On k columns each residual vector contributes one tensored factor acting on all k columns, s_c factors in all. B states it; A only mentions C^{(x)mk} on k columns as the endpoint result, not the factor count.

Endpoint frames: the zero label has frame I and the full label frame C^{(x)m} (so every pair except X_a->Y_a already gets C^{(x)m}). B states this; A carries the X_a->Y_a repair (C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates, Z_{a,k} before, i^{27k} Z_{a,k} after, negated X outputs) but not the zero/full-label endpoint frames.

items.note: P1 and P2 are present in both. B carries P3 and the full P4; A lacks P3 and the endpoint-frame part of P4.
Both carry R1 (L/N<1/2, deficits N-2L_b and 2N-2L_c, s<Wm), R2, R3 and R4 (deficits above 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-eta), tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}) (paper 1105-1110, 1319-1343).
Both state the four elementary stream operations and the controlled shift by splitting each fiber at the offset, with unit multiplication and negation in O(V) (paper 491-639).

differences.what: Elimination proof of A=E_1 Pi E_2: A states the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing left and below by lower-triangular elementary matrices, scaling, deleting the pivot row and column and repeating; B states only the pivot choice and that Pi has a ones.
B states the conjugation order of the shear (transform D by E_2 and H by E_1^{-1}, add Pi D, transform back); A does not.

items.note: M2, M3 and M4 are present in both. A carries the checklist sub-step M1 fully where B has it only in part; B's extra conjugation order is a lesser detail.

Both carry the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, edge shears by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three-shear interchange, s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved to O(e^tau), and the fixed-tape parking schedule with descriptor bound (paper 1491-1616).

Both take rho high digits as a row field of range at least W^k, pad rows, split the rest in base m with a geometric sum, pad binary ranges to q^e, and handle widths differing by one bit (paper 1649-1762); A adds the field-order sequence, which is not decisive.

Both state the C identities, P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}, the slot layout with s_c child calls on f=e/m axes, the inverse-child identity, the row-addition count and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D (paper 1814-1940).

differences.what: The omitted top selected position j_{f-1} is handled by one two-bit XOR in O(V), and for f=1 this is the whole algorithm; A notes the segments lie below the top position but never says how that position is processed.

items.note: Both carry the eight updates and parity cycles, the packed cyclic shifts, the guard interval and bad set, the union bound, the T_0 S_0^{-1} correction by extraction and radix sort, and the cost. B adds the one case of the top selected position.

Both carry q_0, k_0, the row index with padding, the 1/W role split, beta=1/2, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal-node and leaf sums and the base-m partition giving O(d^{lambda'}) (paper 2286-2448).

differences.what: Uniformity of the packed calls in the proof: R_g=2r(p+2Delta+3)<=12rp, A_*<=C_A p with C_A=C_M+b_r+7, and the two normalized extra terms tending to zero uniformly. A carries these; B omits them.

items.note: S1 to S5 are present in both. A additionally carries the proof's verification that every packed child has the required cost uniformly over the parameter bands.

Both carry character cancellation without division, decimation in frequency with bit-reversed storage, the reversed procedure, the multi-axis round H then J_E, the layout L with prefix moves and chunk exchanges and its costs, and the per-round truncation error (paper 2819-3206). Small extras on each side (A defines F^-+; B notes H_0^2=I/2) balance.
Both carry B_0=2^{4p}, the 4pr-bit evaluations, |h_j|<B_0/2 with centered residues and carry, the negacyclic reduction, the truncating shift and the four-product cost (paper 3233-3368).
Both use the retained LB order with pointwise products commuting, the normalization identity, the error chain to sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} and the cost (paper 3414-3495).

differences.what: Definition of the retained permutations (P_s u)_j=u_{tj} and (P_t v)_k=v_{-sk}: A states them; B uses R and Q without ever defining P_s, P_t.
Explicit Gaussian maps S and T (their kernels): A states them; B names them without formulas.

items.note: Both carry N=CTD with the Neumann inversion, the normalizations, A and B_0 as contractions, the numerical maps, the avoided sorts and the tensor interface with axis exposure. A also defines the permutations and the Gaussian maps.
Both state the chirp, its period, the coefficient comparison giving QF_t u, F_s^+R=R^{-1}F_s^+ from t_i a unit mod s_i, and (u*v)/S^2 (paper 3938-3988).

differences.what: Verification that the fixed constants satisfy the layer conditions (tau(1+c/beta)<1-31*2^{-55}<lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)=1-2^{-51}<lambda<lambda'<1) and the dimension conditions on epsilon; A lists the constants without these checks.
The band constants a_d=a_r=1/12, b_d=1, b_r=1/3, C_l=1 from b/2<=log_2 T<=b, fixing the hypotheses of the layer and transform lemmas; A omits them.

items.note: Both carry the constants, sizes, alpha, gamma, eta, the prime-interval bound, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p and the search cost. B adds the checks that the constants satisfy every lemma's conditions and the band constants.
Both state Phi, its isomorphism argument, the triangular coordinate formula, the padded rotations with order i=d..1, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost (paper 4216-4296).
Both state Theta, its well-definedness and isometry, the wrap factor zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T and the computed twist (paper 4298-4413).
Both give the chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart RF_s, the conjugate opposite procedure and the six steps with the two scalings by S (paper 4415-4544).
Both chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L and the final 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, then rounding and carries (paper 4546-4806).
Both carry the cost table, the seven margins with minimum 2^{-181}=2 kappa, the per-row justifications, o(V) setup and exceptional streams, and the cutoff (paper 4810-4995).

differences.what: The negation of the eventual lower bound needs one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0, and the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) bound makes the ratio tend to zero through all lengths. B states this; A's S1 gives only the historical setting.

items.note: Only B carries the logical step from the time bound to disproving the conjecture in this model.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: the restoring exchange network, frames, nested labels with only central 3->4 losses, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b and s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c below Wm, the deficits giving tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, the recurrences F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), then the transforms, convolution, resampling, recovery and cost table with kappa=2^{-182}. Neither chain thins out or breaks where the other does not.

errors.says: Over F_2 every nonzero residual is nonalternating because it contains a coordinate unit vector of norm one.
errors.paper: The norm-one vector in each residual is built by tensoring norm-one vectors chosen in each summand, including the line vectors spanning P and Q, which are not coordinate units; the residual need not contain a coordinate unit vector (e.g. P(x)F(x)Q).

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both carry the central chain the same way. On the core checklist items B carries sub-steps A lacks: the per-edge residual table (L1) and a correct L4 for the labels, and the k-column factor count (P3) and the zero/full-label endpoint frames (P4) for the phase interface. B also carries the conjecture-negation step. A's advantages are smaller completeness details (the full elimination in M1, the uniform packed-cost check in the layer proof, the definitions of P_s and P_t), and A has one minor misstatement in L4.
